title: Distribution with prescribed Fourier mean
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. Write $\widehat f(S)$ for the Fourier–Walsh coefficient of $f$ at $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $L=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}|\widehat f(S)|$. If $L>0$, there is a probability distribution $\pi$ on the subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that, for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the expectation over $S\sim\pi$ of $\operatorname{sgn}_+(\widehat f(S))\chi_S(x)$ equals $f(x)/L$, where $\operatorname{sgn}_+(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
the sum of the absolute Fourier–Walsh coefficients of $f$ is positive
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. Write $\operatorname{sgn}_+(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$. For a real cube function $f$ with $L=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|\widehat f(S)|>0$, there exists a probability distribution $\pi$ on the subsets of $[n]$ such that $\mathbb E_{S\sim\pi}[\operatorname{sgn}_+(\widehat f(S))\chi_S(x)]=f(x)/L$ for every cube point $x$.
